correctness.rationale: For all R,T>0 the Markov generator for (X,S), S in {-1,0,1}, gives m_k=h_(k-1), (k-1+R)h_(k-1)=(k-1)u_(k-2), and (k+R+T)u_k=(k+T)m_k. At even k these imply m_(2j)/m_(2j-2)=(2j-1)(T+2j-2)/[(R+2j-1)(R+T+2j-2)], with m0=1 and m2=T/[(R+1)(R+T)]. Hence Q_n is exactly the stated product for every integer n>=2. Its log derivative is sum of d_R(T+2j-2)-d_R(T), where d_R(x)=R/[x(x+R)] strictly decreases, so Q_n strictly decreases. As T->0, Q_n~const*T^(1-n)->infinity; as T->infinity, Q_n tends to product_(j=2)^n (R+1)/(R+2j-1)<1. Thus a unique positive root exists with the claimed signs. The n=2 identity reduces to R^2+R-RT-T^2-2T=0 and the stated positive root. Gamma products yield m2n~[c Gamma((R+1)/2)Gamma(R/2)/(2sqrt(pi))]n^(-(R+1)) at T=c/n, while (2n-1)!!m2^n~sqrt(2)e^(-c/R)[2c/(eR(R+1))]^n. Uniformity for c in compact positive intervals brackets c_n=nT_n and the root expansion gives c_n=c_R[1-((R+1)log n-B_R)/n+O_R((log n)^2/n^2)]. This is for fixed R>0 only. Independently reconstructed an exact conditional-state generator solution and compared 60 rational moment cases through degree 30, simplified two symbolic fourth-cumulant/root identities, and solved 12 high-precision roots for R=0.2,1,3 and n=20,100,1000,10000. Their error behavior corroborates (not proves) the analytic asymptotic. The source tree was independently recomputed from its seven actual Git blob SHAs and matches the assigned tree.
residual_risks: Numerical root tests are finite and cannot prove the n->infinity result; correctness relies on the independent gamma Stirling and bracketing derivation.
No uniform conclusion for R depending on n, R approaching zero or infinity, Brownian forcing or nonexponential rests.

value.rationale: The stationary three-state harmonic particle is a natural physical stochastic model and variance-matched Gaussian excess is a natural nondimensional measure of high-order non-Gaussianity. Exactly one sign change for every even order n>=2 gives a full qualitative phase classification over a continuous two-rate family. The sharp nT_n limit and (log n)/n displacement identify a singular order-dependent boundary not available by a fixed-order kurtosis sign calculation; a researcher can use the exact boundary to distinguish long-rest intermittency at increasing moment sensitivity. The all-n asymptotic and exact uniqueness are substantive information rather than renaming a known table or merely enumerating small cases. This is a natural derived structural theorem, not an assertion of distributional dominance or novel raw moments.
residual_risks: Moment sign thresholds may be difficult to estimate in finite samples because high even moments are statistically unstable.
Physical interpretation is limited to exact stationary expectations and no assertion of full tail or convex stochastic order is supported.

limitations: Original stationary law and arbitrary even-moment recurrence are known from Sun–Ye–Podgornik; n=2 fourth-kurtosis threshold is also previously published. Originality acceptance is restricted to full hierarchy plus sharp singular asymptotic.
